passages.title: SCUT-FBP5500: A Diverse Benchmark Dataset for Multi-Paradigm Facial Beauty Prediction
passages.method_and_sample: Dataset construction and predictive benchmarking; 5,500 images, 60 raters.
passages.limitations: Dataset collected mostly from the Internet; consent/identity deduplication is not established here. Frontal-face and rater-population limits apply. No per-component beauty or occlusion labels. Non-commercial research only.
passages.text: The authors introduce 5,500 frontal face images, overall beauty ratings on a 1-5 scale from 60 volunteers, and 86 manually annotated facial landmarks. The benchmark supports regression, classification and ranking. ResNet-18 is one reported baseline.

passages.title: Machine Learning-Based Facial Beauty Prediction and Analysis of Frontal Facial Images Using Facial Landmarks and Traditional Image Descriptors
passages.method_and_sample: Feature ablations and supervised beauty prediction on 5,500 frontal faces.
passages.limitations: Abstract/metadata verified through publisher-deposited Crossref record; full article not indexed. Correlations on one benchmark do not establish a universal golden-ratio rule or component scores.
passages.text: The study compares geometric ratios and traditional texture, shape and HSV color descriptors on 5,500 frontal images. It trains KNN, linear regression, random forest and a neural network. Its abstract reports improved prediction when landmarks and other descriptors are combined.
passages.keywords: beauty symmetry texture ratios color landmarks

passages.title: Grad-CAM: Visual Explanations from Deep Networks via Gradient-based Localization
passages.method_and_sample: Gradient-based localization; image classification and visual reasoning tasks.
passages.limitations: A heatmap reflects model sensitivity; it is not a causal proof or a calibrated beauty score for an eye, nose or lip. The original paper concerns visual explanation benchmarks, not QMA Face validation.
passages.text: Grad-CAM uses gradients flowing into a convolutional layer to produce a coarse localization map of regions relevant to a network output. It can be applied to existing convolutional networks without training a separate explanation model.
passages.keywords: grad cam explanation attribution heatmap model

passages.title: DeepGeoFusion: personalized facial beauty prediction through geometric-visual fusion
passages.method_and_sample: Visual-geometric fusion and personalized beauty experiments on SCUT-FBP5500.
passages.limitations: Published model results are not results of our engine. External landmark requirements and multi-module implementation must be considered under our two-model deployment limit. No component label dataset is supplied here.
passages.text: This paper combines visual features with a graph of 86 facial landmarks and an attention-based fusion module. It also describes adaptation to individual aesthetic preferences using user ratings. The publisher lists publication on 15 January 2026, although the DOI contains 2025.
passages.keywords: beauty landmarks geometry personalized geometric fusion

passages.title: Facial attractiveness: evolutionary based research
passages.method_and_sample: Review of experimental and cross-cultural attractiveness literature; no single sample size.
passages.limitations: Research review, not a single scoring dataset or a validation of this app. It does not supply a universal score, diagnoses, character labels or per-component beauty ratings. Only a short original summary is indexed.
passages.text: The review discusses symmetry, average facial shape, skin appearance and variation in attractiveness preferences. It considers visual experience, familiarity and social learning as sources of differences in preferences.
passages.keywords: beauty symmetry preferences skin color individual differences

passages.title: Face evaluation: Findings, methods, and challenges
passages.method_and_sample: Review of face-evaluation studies and individual-participant computational models; no single sample size.
passages.limitations: These are studies of perceived traits and observers judgments, not tests of a photographed persons honesty or actual trustworthiness. Do not turn perception labels into personality predictions.
passages.text: The review examines how observers evaluate faces and how computational methods model those judgments. It emphasizes individual differences that can be obscured by aggregating ratings across observers.
passages.keywords: trustworthiness honesty personality face judgement individual differences

passages.title: Emotional Expressions Reconsidered: Challenges to Inferring Emotion From Human Facial Movements
passages.method_and_sample: Scientific evidence review about anger, disgust, fear, happiness, sadness and surprise; no single sample size.
passages.limitations: Visible movements do not uniquely identify an internal state. This is not a deception, morality or trustworthiness detector. Publisher abstract and a short original summary are indexed, not the paid full article.
passages.text: The review evaluates evidence about six commonly studied emotion categories. It finds substantial variation across people, cultures and situations; a facial movement can communicate more than one emotion or non-emotional information.
passages.keywords: emotion body language context culture movement expression

passages.title: PFLD: A Practical Facial Landmark Detector
passages.method_and_sample: Landmark localization experiments on 300W and AFLW; benchmark performance, not human component ratings.
passages.limitations: Landmark accuracy is not beauty-score accuracy. No PFLD weight is installed: adding a separate detector would exceed the model limit. Claims in the paper require reproduction on our device and data.
passages.text: PFLD proposes an efficient single-stage landmark network with geometry-related training regularization and losses accounting for difficult conditions. The paper evaluates landmark localization on benchmark face datasets and reports a compact mobile implementation.
passages.keywords: landmarks lightweight face pose occlusion points

passages.title: Lightweight Facial Attractiveness Prediction Using Dual Label Distribution
passages.method_and_sample: Dual-label distribution learning with MobileNetV2; two benchmark datasets.
passages.limitations: Version 2 is dated April 2024; the first preprint was 2022. Overall rating distributions are not labels for beauty of individual facial components. Code licensing does not override dataset restrictions.
passages.text: This approach combines attractiveness ratings, mean scores and rating variation into a joint label-distribution learning objective. It uses MobileNetV2 as a lightweight backbone and evaluates attractiveness prediction on two benchmarks.
passages.keywords: beauty lightweight mobilenet dual label distribution

passages.title: Physiognomy in the Age of AI
passages.method_and_sample: Historical and critical discussion; no experimental training sample.
passages.limitations: Book chapter, not a validated face-character classifier. Only this brief original description of its scope is indexed; do not cite it as proof of specific quantitative findings.
passages.text: This critical chapter discusses the history and renewed use of physiognomy in artificial intelligence. It is a source for examining claims about facial appearance and character, rather than a method for analyzing a persons morality.
passages.keywords: physiognomy personality trustworthiness honesty face reading
